reading.body:
Flexential Denver - Downtown claims 759,000 square feet of technical space but publishes no power capacity, making it impossible to assess its role in Colorado's AI infrastructure.

The operator's website lists four other Denver metro facilities by name and location, Aurora, Centennial, Englewood, and Parker, but does not identify this Downtown property as a distinct operating site. Flexential's own marketing materials do not confirm the facility exists as a separate asset or describe its current status. This gap between claimed capacity and public verification complicates any assessment of whether the space is built out, powered, and running compute workloads.

Colorado has 17 mapped data center facilities on record. Only three publish power capacity figures. Those three disclose 26.35 MW total. The state's actual power footprint for AI workloads is almost certainly higher than published figures show, since most operators do not release capacity data. Without disclosure from Flexential, this facility cannot be ranked among the state's capacity constraints or integrated into grid planning models.

Technical square footage alone tells you nothing about power draw, power source, or occupancy. The binding constraint on AI scaling is power, not floor space. A facility this size could draw anywhere from negligible capacity to hundreds of megawatts depending on build-out and utilization. Until the operator publishes a power figure, this asset is invisible to anyone planning Colorado's AI-driven grid expansion.
